title: VOA Learning English - Health Report
titleVi: VOA Learning English - Báo cáo Sức khỏe

transcript.text: Welcome to The Health Report. I'm Ashley Thompson.
Today we're going to talk about a new study on sleep and memory.
Researchers at Stanford University found that people who sleep at least seven hours a night perform better on memory tests.
The study followed over five hundred participants for six months.
Participants were divided into two groups: those who slept eight hours and those who slept six hours.
The results showed that the eight-hour group scored twenty percent higher on average.
Dr. Martinez, the lead researcher, says sleep is essential for consolidating memories.
Without adequate rest, the brain cannot properly process and store new information.
The researchers recommend that adults aim for seven to nine hours of sleep each night.
That's all for today's Health Report. Join us next week for more updates.

title: TED Talk - How to Learn Anything
titleVi: TED Talk - Cách Học Bất Cứ Điều Gì

transcript.text: Thank you so much. It's a pleasure to be here today.
I want to talk about something that changed my life completely.
Five years ago, I decided to learn how to play the guitar.
I had always wanted to play, but I thought I was too old to start.
I was wrong. The truth is, anyone can learn anything at any age.
The key is not talent, but practice and persistence.
I practiced for thirty minutes every single day.
After six months, I could play my first complete song.
After one year, I joined a band and performed at local venues.
The lesson I learned is simple: consistency beats intensity.

title: VOA Learning English - Technology Report
titleVi: VOA Learning English - Báo cáo Công nghệ

transcript.text: Hello and welcome to the Technology Report from VOA Learning English.
Artificial intelligence is changing the way we work and live.
A new report from MIT shows that AI could replace forty percent of jobs in the next decade.
However, the report also emphasizes that AI will create new opportunities.
Jobs in data analysis, machine learning, and robotics are growing rapidly.
Experts advise workers to develop skills in critical thinking and creativity.
These human abilities are difficult for machines to replicate.
The report concludes that continuous learning will be essential for career success.

title: TED-Ed - Why We Study History
titleVi: TED-Ed - Tại Sao Chúng Ta Học Lịch Sử

transcript.text: Have you ever wondered why we study history?
It's not just about memorizing dates and names.
History helps us understand how societies evolved over time.
It teaches us about cause and effect, patterns, and consequences.
By studying the past, we can make better decisions for the future.
History also helps us appreciate different cultures and perspectives.
It reminds us that we are part of a larger human story.

title: VOA Learning English - English in a Minute
titleVi: VOA Learning English - Tiếng Anh Trong Một Phút

transcript.text: Welcome to English in a Minute.
Today's phrase is: to break the ice.
This means to make people feel more comfortable in a social situation.
For example: I told a joke to break the ice at the party.
The phrase comes from the idea of breaking through a barrier.
Try using this phrase in your next conversation.

title: TED Talk - The Power of Curiosity
titleVi: TED Talk - Sức Mạnh Của Sự Tò Mò

transcript.text: Curiosity is one of the most powerful drivers of learning.
When we're curious, our brains release dopamine, which makes learning feel rewarding.
Children are naturally curious, but as we grow older, we often lose that sense of wonder.
The good news is that we can rekindle curiosity by asking questions and exploring new topics.
Studies show that curious people tend to be more creative and better problem-solvers.
So next time you encounter something new, take a moment to ask: why? and how?

title: VOA Learning English - Travel Tips
titleVi: VOA Learning English - Mẹo Du Lịch

transcript.text: Traveling can be exciting but also stressful.
Here are some tips to make your trip smoother.
Always keep your passport and important documents in a safe place.
Make copies of your documents in case you lose the originals.
Learn a few basic phrases in the local language.
This can help you connect with locals and navigate more easily.
Remember to stay hydrated and take breaks during long journeys.

title: TED Talk - Unlocking Creativity
titleVi: TED Talk - Khơi Dậy Sáng Tạo

transcript.text: Creativity is not something you're born with; it's a skill you can develop.
The first step is to embrace curiosity and ask more questions.
Don't be afraid to make mistakes; they are part of the creative process.
Try combining ideas from different fields to create something new.
Take breaks and give your mind time to wander; this often leads to breakthroughs.
Surround yourself with diverse perspectives and experiences.

title: VOA Learning English - Environment Report
titleVi: VOA Learning English - Báo cáo Môi trường

transcript.text: Climate change is one of the biggest challenges facing our planet.
Rising temperatures are causing ice caps to melt and sea levels to rise.
Scientists warn that we need to reduce carbon emissions significantly.
Renewable energy sources like solar and wind power are becoming more affordable.
Individuals can help by reducing waste and conserving energy.
Small changes in our daily habits can make a big difference over time.

title: TED Talk - What Makes a Great Leader
titleVi: TED Talk - Điều Tạo Nên Nhà Lãnh Đạo Giỏi

transcript.text: Great leaders inspire others to achieve their full potential.
They communicate a clear vision and set achievable goals.
Good leaders listen actively and value their team's input.
They lead by example and demonstrate integrity in their actions.
Great leaders also know how to delegate and empower others.
They remain calm under pressure and make thoughtful decisions.
